title: The Tractability Border of Reachability in Simple Vector Addition Systems with States
authors: Dmitry Chistikov (University of Warwick, United Kingdom), Wojciech Czerwiński (University of Warsaw, Poland), Filip Mazowiecki (University of Warsaw, Poland), Łukasz Orlikowski (University of Warsaw, Poland), Henry Sinclair-Banks (University of Warwick, United Kingdom), Karol Węgrzycki (Saarland University and MPI for Informatics, Germany)
abstract: Vector Addition Systems with States (VASS), equivalent to Petri nets, are a well-established model of concurrency. A d-dimensional VASS can be viewed as a directed graph whose edges are labeled by d-dimensional integer vectors. As a path is followed, the values of d nonnegative integer counters are updated according to these integer labels. The central algorithmic challenge in VASS is the reachability problem: can a run be made from a given starting node and counter values to a specified target node and counter values? When the input is encoded in binary, reachability is computationally intractable: even in dimension one, it is NP-hard. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive characterization of the tractability boundary for the problem when the input is encoded in unary. Our main result proves that reachability is NP-hard in unary-encoded 3-dimensional VASS, even when the structure is restricted to a simple linear-path scheme. This improves on a recent result by Czerwiński and Orlikowski [LICS 2022], in both the number of counters and the expressiveness of the considered model, and answers open questions raised by Englert, Lazić, and Totzke [LICS 2016], as well as Leroux [PETRI NETS 2021]. The underlying graph structure of a simple linear path scheme (SLPS) is merely a path with self-loops at each node. We also investigate the exceedingly weak model of computation that is SLPS with counter updates restricted to the values {-1, 0, +1}. In this case, we show that reachability remains NP-hard when the dimension is bounded by O(α(k)), where α is the inverse Ackermann function and k bounds the size of the SLPS. We complement this result by presenting a polynomial-time algorithm that decides reachability in 2-dimensional SLPS when the initial and target configurations are specified in binary. To achieve this, we demonstrate that reachability in such instances has a well-structured nature: all loops, except possibly a constant number, are either taken a polynomial number of times or nearly maximally. This extends the main result of Englert, Lazić, and Totzke [LICS 2016], who showed the problem is in NL when the initial and target configurations are specified in unary.
